privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Neura AI respects your privacy. This app does not send your data to any server — everything is stored only on this device.

sections.p: Your name, questionnaire answers, and game results are stored only in your device's browser storage (localStorage). This data is never sent to us or any third party.
No registration, email, or password is required. There is no cloud storage — your data never leaves your device.

For a memory game, random face photos (randomuser.me) and fonts (Google Fonts) are loaded. When opened inside Telegram, the Telegram WebApp SDK runs. These requests may receive your IP address as part of normal internet operation.
The app contains no analytics, advertising, or third-party trackers.
The "Delete account" button on the profile page instantly and permanently removes all your local data.

common.livesNote: You have 3 lives — the game ends after 3 mistakes
common.quitBody: The current round won't be saved. Completed rounds are kept.

rules.schulte: Find the numbers in order, starting from 1. A found number vanishes and a bigger one appears. Find as many as you can before time runs out.
rules.memory: Memorize the lit cells, then tap them. Find them all correctly → next, harder stage.
rules.stroop: Ignore the color of the letters. Pick the color by the WORD's meaning (what it says). Be fast and accurate.
rules.speed: Tap the side the arrow points to — as fast as you can.
rules.math: Solve the problem and choose the correct answer. Fast and accurate.
rules.sequence: If the current cell matches the one a few steps back — press 'MATCH'. Working memory.
rules.nebula: Memorize the lit targets. They move — when they stop, pick which ones were targets.
rules.audioMemory: Memorize the sequence of sounds and repeat it in the same order.
rules.names: Link faces and names. Then answer 'Who is this?' with the correct name.
rules.pictogram: Memorize the shown symbols, then find them in the grid.
rules.iq: Find the rule in the number sequence and choose the next number.
rules.crossword: Build the word matching the clue from the letters, then check.
rules.eyeHand: Tap the lit cell as fast as you can — eye-hand coordination.
rules.fingerDance: Tap the lit panels fast and in the right order — finger speed.
rules.palmClash: Tap the lit side in rhythm — coordination.
rules.neuroSync: Tap the cell exactly on time — synchrony.
rules.mirrorDraw: Tap the lit cell and its mirrored (symmetric) twin.
rules.focusShift: Focus alternately on near and far points — eye exercise (no cognitive score).
rules.rule202020: Every 20 minutes look ~6 m (20 ft) away for 20 seconds — eye rest (no cognitive score).
rules.figureEight: Follow the dot with your eyes, drawing a figure 8 in the air — eye exercise (no cognitive score).

recs.title: A plan for your brain
recs.intro: Tailored to your answers. Every recommendation is grounded in real neuroscience research.
recs.honest: This is general scientific consensus, not personal medical advice. Sources are shown openly.

sleep.title: Sleep consolidates memory
sleep.body: Aim for 7–9 hours. Sleep consolidates what you learned during the day.

exercise.title: Movement feeds the brain
exercise.body: Aerobic exercise 3+ times a week benefits hippocampal volume and cognition.
exercise.source: Hillman, Erickson & Kramer, 2008, Nature Reviews Neuroscience

nutrition.title: Brain food
nutrition.body: Omega-3 and a Mediterranean diet support cognitive health.

mental.title: Cognitive reserve
mental.body: Learning new skills and staying mentally active builds 'cognitive reserve'.

oxygen.title: Oxygen fuels the brain
oxygen.body: The brain uses ~20% of the body's energy. Fresh air, ventilation and deep breathing support attention.

earlyWake.title: Wake early and consistently
earlyWake.body: Waking at the same time strengthens your circadian rhythm, improving daytime focus and mood.

training.title: The honest truth about training
training.body: Practice improves the trained task; 'you'll get generally smarter' is not proven.
training.source: Simons et al., 2016; Owen et al., 2010, Nature

stress.title: Chronic stress
stress.body: Prolonged stress raises cortisol and damages the hippocampus, the memory center.

sugar.title: Too much sugar
sugar.body: A high-sugar diet lowers BDNF and hippocampal function, weakening learning.

sleepLoss.title: Staying up at night
sleepLoss.body: Sleep loss sharply reduces attention, memory and decision-making.

processed.title: Artificial / ultra-processed foods
processed.body: Higher ultra-processed food (UPF) intake is linked to faster cognitive decline.
processed.source: Gomes Gonçalves et al., 2023, JAMA Neurology

memory.name: Memory
memory.fact: Working memory — the Baddeley & Hitch model (1974): the brain temporarily holds and manipulates information. Targeted practice raises holding capacity and accuracy.
memory.source: Baddeley & Hitch, 1974; Klingberg, 2010, Trends in Cognitive Sciences

attention.name: Attention
attention.fact: Attention is not one thing — it spans alerting, orienting and executive-control networks (Posner & Petersen, 1990). Visual search trains directed attention.
attention.source: Posner & Petersen, 1990, Annual Review of Neuroscience

logic.name: Logic
logic.fact: Fluid intelligence (Gf) is the ability to solve novel problems without prior knowledge (Cattell, 1963). Logic drills engage this process.

speed.name: Speed
speed.fact: Processing speed declines naturally with age (Salthouse, 1996), but rapid-decision drills sharpen reaction time.

focus.name: Inhibition
focus.fact: The Stroop effect (1935) — inhibiting an automatic response — is a measure of executive control (Miyake et al., 2000). It is holding attention against interference.
focus.source: Stroop, 1935; Miyake et al., 2000, Cognitive Psychology

motor.name: Motor & Hands
motor.fact: Complex finger movements activate the motor cortex and cerebellum; bimanual (two-hand) coordination trains cross-hemisphere communication.
motor.source: Doyon & Benali, 2005, Current Opinion in Neurobiology

vision.name: Eye Exercises
vision.fact: The 20-20-20 rule (every 20 minutes look ~6 m (20 ft) away for 20 seconds) is recommended to reduce digital eye strain. This is for eye comfort, not cognitive training.
